annotations_emitted.epistemic_warrant_citation: Brasier, M.D. et al. (1994). Decision on the Precambrian-Cambrian boundary stratotype. Episodes, 17(1-2), 3-8.
annotations_emitted.rationale: Standard PBDB body fossil tables capture only N=5 occurrences (4 taxa) for Cambrian infaunal burrowers due to soft-tissue preservation limits. Yet global trace fossils (Treptichnus pedum, Arenicolites) document rapid vertical substrate ingress expanding from 1.5mm to 45mm in the Fortunian and 120mm by Stage 5. Fitting diversity-dependent speciation (Gl) strictly on body occurrences produces an artificial Gl=-0.031 driven by missing skeletonized parts rather than ecological carrying capacity.
annotations_emitted.recommended_action: In downstream birth-death models, weight infaunal carrying capacity by stratigraphic burrow depth (mm) or use joint trace-body occurrence priors rather than naive body fossil counts.

annotations_emitted.epistemic_warrant_citation: Ivantsov, A.Y. (2013). Trace fossils of precambrian metazoans. Gondwana Research, 23(3), 850-862.
annotations_emitted.rationale: Sedentary filter feeders (Brachiopoda, Porifera) possess dense biomineralized calcite and siliceous spicules, yielding a high sampling ratio (3.04 occ/taxon). Their negative diversity-dependence (Gl=-0.089) represents a robust physical signature of 2D benthic substrate competition and spatial overgrowth.
annotations_emitted.recommended_action: Uncalibrated PBDB body fossil frequencies are representative for primary inference.
